item.title: Did You Invoice This Month's Hours? The Motorway Services
item.description: Parked at a motorway services, phone in hand, you can't remember if you invoiced this month's hours. A freelancer's story about the calmer way.

item.title: Can't Remember Invoices You Sent? The Coffee Machine
item.description: A client's accountant asks which invoice you meant, and you don't know what you've sent. A calm story about knowing where every invoice stands.

item.title: The Check Is in the Mail Again? A Freelancer's Wait
item.description: Your client says the check is in the mail, for the third time. A quiet story about waiting at the mailbox and chasing money without feeling like you're begging.

item.title: Client Says 'Next Week' Every Week? The Balcony Tomatoes
item.description: Your client says they'll pay next week, and has said it for six weeks. A quiet story about the Monday you stop waiting and start following a calm plan.

item.title: Client Sent No Brief but Wants It Tomorrow? Farm Shop Box
item.description: No brief, no files, and a client who wants results tomorrow. A freelancer's Thursday at a farm shop, and a calmer way to begin next time.

item.title: Client Sent a Rude Email? The Tailor's Pins and a Pause
item.description: The email was short, cold and unfair, and you read it standing on a tailor's footstool. A calm story about answering a rude client without losing your head.

item.title: Messy CSV Export Every Week? The Conference Coffee Line
item.description: The same messy CSV lands in your inbox every week, and every week you fix it by hand. A short story about the Monday it stopped being your job.

item.title: Forgot to Bill a Client Last Month? The Flea Market Sunday
item.description: You're holding a vase at a flea market when it hits you: last month's job was never invoiced. What that moment feels like, and how it stops happening.

item.title: No Contract or Brief, Work Already Started? The Dog Walk
item.description: Tuesday, 7:30, rain on the lead: the client is already sending files and nothing is in writing. A calm look at how it feels, and what changes.

item.title: Interview Tomorrow, Can't Remember What You Sent Them?
item.description: Interview at 10 tomorrow, and you can't recall which CV or cover letter you sent. A quiet story about walking in prepared instead of guessing.

item.title: Stall Cash Doesn't Match Sales? The Tailgate at 5:10
item.description: The cash tin is short, the notebook says otherwise, and the car is half packed. A market maker's quiet moment at the tailgate, and a calmer way to end the day.

item.title: Haven't Kept Any Receipts This Year? The Hut Terrace
item.description: October, a mountain terrace, and one text that makes you realise you kept no receipts all year. A calm story for freelancers who feel behind.

item.title: Scheduled Backup Failed? The Folder With No Recent Files
item.description: You open the backup folder to find a file for a client and the newest one is months old. A calm story about that drop in your stomach, and what comes after.

item.title: Angry Customer Email? How to Reply: The Bakery Counter
item.description: An angry customer email lands at 8:05 on a Monday and your stomach drops. A calm story about replying without panic, defensiveness or three lost hours.

item.title: Buy Planners, Never Stick With Them? The ADHD Drawer
item.description: Four planners, all abandoned by February. A quiet story for freelancers with busy brains who keep starting over, and what a lighter page can change.

item.title: Forgot Which Projects You Invoiced? The Flower Stall
item.description: Saturday market, a bunch of tulips, and one question you can't answer: did you invoice that project? A calm story about knowing, not guessing.

item.title: Client Ignoring Your Invoice Email? Ticket Number 247
item.description: Your follow-up email sits unanswered and the invoice is weeks late. A quiet story about what to do next, without begging or panicking.

item.title: Client Paid Half My Invoice, Now Silent? The Jetty at Noon
item.description: Half the money arrived, then silence. A Sunday on a rented rowing boat, one unanswered email, and a calmer way to follow up without begging.

item.title: Payment 'Coming' but Nothing Arrives? The Fuel Pump
item.description: Your client swears the payment is on its way, but the account says otherwise. A calm story about what to say next, and how to stop dreading it.

item.title: CSV Column Names Change Every Export? The Park Bench
item.description: Every export brings new column names and blank rows. A lunch-break story about Priya, a sandwich, and the weekly file that never looks the same twice.

item.title: Had to Cancel a Customer's Order? The Choir Break Text
item.description: A customer ordered something you didn't have, and now you have to cancel. A quiet story about that hot-faced moment and how it stops repeating.

item.title: Freelance Receipts a Mess in December? The Advent Door
item.description: It's December, your receipts are in a carrier bag, and you don't know where to start. A quiet Monday-morning story about a calmer way into year-end.

item.title: Dreading a Difficult Client Email? The Fitting Room
item.description: The client's email sits unanswered while you wait behind a fitting room curtain. For freelancers who don't know what to say, and how that knot can loosen.

item.title: Rate Too Low for Taxes and Holidays? The Museum Café
item.description: A friend mentions her paid holiday and your stomach drops. Does your freelance hourly rate cover taxes and time off? A quiet story about finding out.

item.title: Messy CSV Exports Every Week? The Cabin Draining Board
item.description: Half-term in a rented cabin, laptop on the draining board, and the same messy CSV to fix by hand again. A story for anyone who loses hours to exports.

item.title: New Freelance Client, No Idea How to Start? The Egg Queue
item.description: The yes arrives while you queue for eggs. Now what? A calm story about starting a new freelance client project without winging it.

item.title: New Freelance Client, No Process? The Porridge Monday
item.description: A new client says 'let's start Monday' and your process is scattered emails and guesswork. A short story about a calmer first week.

item.title: Parents Pay Tutoring Late? The Half-Term Zoo Queue
item.description: Parents keep paying late and asking feels awkward? A tutor stands in a zoo queue, trying to remember who owes what. A calmer way to see it.

item.title: Students Forget to Pay for Lessons? The 12:50 Sandwich
item.description: Four minutes between two video lessons, a sandwich going dry, and a question you can't ask: who hasn't paid? A story for private tutors.

item.title: Forgot Travel Time in Your Quote? The Ring Road at 7:55
item.description: You quoted the job and forgot the driving. Now every trip across town eats your margin. A calm story about spotting it, and quoting differently next time.

item.title: Recruiter Called, Forgot You Applied? The Cloakroom Ticket
item.description: The recruiter says your name warmly. You have no idea which job she means. A short story about that blank moment, and what a calmer job search feels like.

item.title: Selling Lots of Handmade Items but No Real Profit?
item.description: Parcels go out every day, the stall sells well, yet the account stays thin. A story for makers who can't tell if they're really earning anything.

item.title: Out of Stock Too Late Again? The Café Lids at 7:20 am
item.description: Seven twenty, the queue is out the door, and the lids are gone. A short story for anyone who always finds out too late that something is out of stock.

item.title: Billed the Same Week Twice? The Cheese Counter Ticket
item.description: You think you billed the same week twice and can't tell which hours are invoiced. A quiet story about a Saturday queue, two PDFs, and getting calm back.

item.title: Scattered Data Scripts? The Shoe Repair Counter
item.description: Three chores, three half-remembered scripts, and a Monday morning at a shoe repair counter. A story for developers tired of rebuilding the same tools.

item.title: Need a Tracker for Every Problem? The Bus Shelter Call
item.description: One file for invoices, another for hours, a third for prices, and none of them talk. A quiet story about finally having one calm place for it all.

item.title: Can't Track Job Applications? The Noodle Stall Email
item.description: An interview invite arrives and you can't remember the company. A lunchtime story for anyone losing track of job applications and who replied.

item.title: Forgot Which Jobs You Applied To? The Tram Stop Voicemail
item.description: A recruiter calls back and you can't place the company. If you've lost track of which jobs you applied to and followed up on, this story is for you.

item.title: Client Agreed to Pay but Keeps Making Excuses? Freelancer
item.description: They said yes, they'll pay. Then came the excuses. A quiet story about a Thursday pickup line, and how chasing money can feel calmer.

item.title: Client Ignoring Overdue Reminders? The Ice Rink Bench
item.description: Three reminders sent, three times silence. On a cold rink bench, a freelancer finds a calmer way to chase an overdue invoice. A short story.

item.title: Client Keeps Promising to Pay? The Library Printer Queue
item.description: "Payment goes out Friday." Three Fridays later, nothing. A quiet story for freelancers whose client keeps promising to pay and never does.

item.title: Client Promised to Pay Twice, Still Nothing? What to Say
item.description: They said Friday. Then 'next week, for sure.' Still nothing. A quiet story about the third message and how to send it without feeling like you're begging.

item.title: Client Promised to Pay Friday, Three Fridays Ago?
item.description: Friday again and no payment. A story about the third 'I'll pay on Friday' reply, and what changes when chasing stops feeling like begging.

item.title: Vague Client Feedback Email? The Baggage Carousel Reply
item.description: The email says 'not quite there, make it pop.' You're at a baggage carousel with no idea what to answer. A calm story about replying anyway.

item.title: Overdue Invoice Follow-Up Without Sounding Desperate
item.description: You're in the cheese queue, the invoice is 19 days late, and every email draft sounds either grovelling or furious. There's a calmer way to follow up.

item.title: Freelance Finances a Mess? The Tyre Fitter's Waiting Area
item.description: Your freelance money feels like a mess and you don't know where to start. A quiet story from a tyre garage waiting room, and a calmer way in.

item.title: No Idea What to Earn Next Year? The Mulled Wine Queue
item.description: Dreading January because you don't know how much you need to earn next year? A quiet story from a Christmas market queue, and a calmer way to look at 2027.

item.title: Invoiced the Same Hours Twice? The Red Light at 8:42
item.description: You think you billed the same hours twice. A freelancer's story from a pedestrian crossing, and how a calmer Monday feels when your hours and invoices line up.

item.title: Music Students Cancel Late and Don't Pay? The Guitar Shop
item.description: Your phone buzzes at the shop till: another late cancellation. And who still owes you for March? A music teacher's quiet moment of clarity.

item.title: Nail Tech: How Much Do I Actually Make After Booth Rent?
item.description: The rental form asks for your monthly income and you freeze. A nail tech story about booth rent, products and finding the number you actually keep.
